title: Lejos de + infinitivo: corregir una idea equivocada

sections.content: Lejos de + infinitive (far from doing X) opens a sentence by rejecting a natural but wrong assumption before giving the real picture -- exactly what pre-revolutionary Cuba needs, since "poor, backward island" isn't the accurate starting point. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Lejos de ser uno de los países más pobres de la región, Cuba contaba con uno de los ingresos per cápita más altos de América Latina.
items.english: Far from being one of the region's poorest countries, Cuba had one of the highest per-capita incomes in Latin America.

items.spanish: Lejos de reflejar una prosperidad ampliamente compartida, esta riqueza convivía con una desigualdad social profunda.
items.english: Far from reflecting widely shared prosperity, this wealth coexisted with deep social inequality.

items.spanish: Lejos de ser una economía plenamente independiente, la de Cuba dependía casi por completo de una cuota especial de exportación de azúcar hacia Estados Unidos.
items.english: Far from being a fully independent economy, Cuba's depended almost entirely on a special sugar export quota to the United States.

items.spanish: Esta combinación reunía, precisamente, las condiciones que analizamos como precondiciones típicas para una revolución genuina.
items.english: This combination brought together precisely the conditions we analyzed as typical preconditions for a genuine revolution.

sections.content: Lejos de always sets up a contrast: state the rejected idea first, then follow with the accurate one, usually introduced by sin embargo or a comma-separated clause, as every example above does.
